newsitem.title: USA: DSP Communications falls on outlook.
newsitem.headline: DSP Communications falls on outlook.

text.p: DSP Communications Inc. stock plunged as much as 44 percent Thursday after the cellular phone component maker said it expected lower revenues for at least one quarter as its customers demand a new generation of products.
DSP stock fell $3.75 to $7 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue. Earlier, the stock traded as low as $6, its lowest price in 18 months.
After the market closed Wednesday, DSP said it expected lower profits and revenues in its second quarter than in the first.

The company also reported net income of $6.13 million, or 13 cents a share, for the first quarter, slightly less than the 14 cents Wall Street was expecting, according to a recent analyst survey by Zacks Investment Research.
DSP makes the chips and software that control the basic functions of cellular phones and telecommunications equipment.
The company supplies Japanese customers with components for cellular phones based on the Personal Digital Cellular, or PDC, standard.
The PDC standard, however, faces competition from the more recently introduced CDMA standard, which is cheaper for cellular service providers to use in their networks.
To keep their customers, PDC phone makers are scrambling for the latest generation of PDC components and buying less of DSP's older PDC products.

"Our production for the second quarter will be reduced due to anticipated phase-out of our existing chip sets, as our customers move to new models," DSP Chief Executive Nathan Hod said in a statement.
Company officials did not return phone calls Thursday.
